correctness.rationale: Every feasible code is a union of two-word reverse-complement orbits among 96 GC-balanced words. The 44 candidate vertices and all 344 shadow conflicts are rebuilt directly. Fourteen explicitly listed conflict cliques cover each vertex at least twice, yielding |I|<=7; a seven-orbit witness attains 14 codewords. An exhaustive increasing-index recursion and an independent C++ bitmask enumerator both give precisely 20 seven-orbit selections, zero eight-orbit selections, and the 4,4,4,8 symmetry split. Complete checker source and data are embedded; finite completeness follows from enumeration of all 4^4 input words and proof of increasing-index traversal.

value.rationale: GC balance, double-strand closure and correction of a deletion model independent concrete DNA-code constraints motivated in the primary literature. Their simultaneous exact four-base capacity is not implied by any one marginal constraint, and the twenty-extremizer/four-symmetry-class classification describes the complete optimal short-code design space; the 14-clique cover explains a sharp capacity obstruction. The claim makes no downstream biological efficacy assertion.
